payload.author: CharlesNaig
payload.body:
### What do you want added?

Dangling CNAME - subdomain takeover
When a user registers a CNAME record pointing to, e.g., name.vercel.app, the validator does not check whether that target host is actually claimed/alive. If the user later abandons their Vercel project but the domain file stays in the repo, anyone can register the same Vercel app name and take over name.is-a.dev. This enables phishing, cookie theft, CSRF bypass, CSP bypass, and OAuth token hijack under a trusted *.is-a.dev origin.

What fix could we take with this? I just noticed this is a security issue, so I suggesting something like an auto-checker app.

- It adds unnecessary noise to commits.  
- It's specific to local development environments and not relevant to the project itself.

payload.author: wdhdev
payload.body:
###### (reference #13995)

---

# Alternatives

## [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/application-services/products/dns/)
- **Pros**
	- Free, up until certain limits
	- Cloudflare proxy option
	- Caching via Cloudflare's global CDN (when proxy is enabled)
	- Faster DNS deployment
	- Built-in DDoS protection for subdomains (when proxy is enabled)
	- NS record support for subdomains
	- Free email forwarding (can setup support@is-a.dev, security@is-a.dev, etc)
	- Cloudflare Zero Trust
		- Tunnels
- **Cons**
	- Record limit, although can be increased by contacting support I believe
	- Not great support

## [Bunny.net](https://bunny.net/pricing/dns/)
- **Pros**
	- Good support
	- Custom/whitelabel nameserver support (e.g. ns1.is-a.dev & ns2.is-a.dev show as the nameserver records, but Bunny.net is the backend)
	- DNS query logs and statistics
	- Importing zone file
- **Cons**
	- Paid
	- Limit of 20 million queries a month, before it's paid
![image](https://github.com/is-a-dev/register/assets/87287585/39748467-807e-44c4-92a0-55b91e563a72)
    - No NS record support (also has limited records types available, compared to Cloudflare)

---

## Overall cons
- Moving CI over could be a hassle, however using [DNSControl](https://dnscontrol.org) could make it easier. (used with Open Domains and Free Domains)
- URL records, not sure how we would manage to implement these, but we could figure out a way.
payload.title: Moving to another DNS provider
